The single most heavily bombed country in history, per head of population, was never at war with the United States.

Every country bombed by the US since 1946 — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ That country is Laos. Between 1964 and 1973 US aircraft dropped somewhere around two million tonnes of ordnance on it, most of it aimed at supply routes running to Vietnam. Laos was formally neutral throughout.

2/ A commonly cited way to picture it: roughly one planeload of bombs every eight minutes, day and night, for nine years. Up to a third of the cluster submunitions failed to detonate, and they are still being cleared today.

3/ Korea comes first chronologically. By 1953 the US had dropped several hundred thousand tonnes on the peninsula. Air Force commander Curtis LeMay later said they had burned down every town in North Korea, and much of the South as well.

4/ Notice how much of the red is in a band from West Africa across to Southeast Asia, and almost none in Europe or the Americas south of Panama. That band is roughly the Cold War's proxy zone plus the post-2001 counterterrorism map, laid on top of each other.
5/ The Americas aren't empty though. Guatemala 1954, Cuba 1961, Panama 1989, Grenada 1983 — small, short, and mostly forgotten outside the countries they happened in.

6/ Europe has exactly one entry: Yugoslavia, 1999. Seventy-eight days of NATO strikes over Kosovo, run without a UN Security Council mandate. It remains the argument that everyone reaches for, in both directions, whenever intervention comes up.

7/ A map like this flattens very different things — a decade-long campaign and a single cruise missile get the same colour. Worth remembering as you read it. What it does show is reach: no other state has ever had this one.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
